title: Spacecraft Fire Experiment-II

sources.title: The Spacecraft Fire Experiment (Saffire) - Objectives, Development and Status
Buoyancy Effects on Concurrent Flame Spread Over Thick PMMA

key_findings: Determined microgravity flammability limits for several spacecraft materials
Examined how microgravity and limited oxygen affect flame size
fields.earth_applications: Studying fire in small, sealed environments such as the Cygnus cargo supply vehicle benefits fire safety and prevention efforts on Earth, including inside mines, airplanes, or submarines.

conditions.label: PMMA samples, low-gravity combustion
evidence: The Saffire-II was conducted at an air flow velocity of either 20 or 30 cm/s

conditions.label: Saffire-III samples, normal gravity
evidence: while Saffire-III will be run at a flow velocity of 30 cm/s

conditions.label: Normal gravity, varying pressure
evidence: Experiments in normal gravity were conducted over pressures ranging between 100 and 40 kPa and a forced flow velocity of 200 mm/s.

conditions.label: Microgravity, fixed pressure and flow speed
evidence: Microgravity experiments were conducted during NASA’s Spacecraft Fire Experiment (Saffire II), on board the Cygnus spacecraft at 100 kPa with an air flow velocity of 200 mm/s.

paper_findings.text: The materials selected for Saffire-II have normal gravity Maximum Oxygen Concentration (MOC) flammability limits that indicate they will burn in normal gravity just above and below 21% O2 by volume.
Reductions of pressure slow down the flame spread over the PMMA surface approaching that in microgravity.

At an ambient pressure of 100 kPa, the pyrolysis front takes about 150 s to progress over the entire length of the sample (~140 mm), which is significantly faster when compared to the average 450 s obtained at about 40 kPa.
The flame brightness is also reduced with pressure, becoming weaker as pressure is reduced.
